items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: We became great friends afterwards and still are.

ctx.x: I was on vacation and not looking for work, beside I hadn't blown for quite a while, but I was really happy to have been engaged for this session, which was the only time I really wanted to play during my visit to the Apple. The Lion was a regular must at the Plaza and I was told that he was there for every session. I was happy playing with my ole buddy Dickie Wells and the rest of the fellows and they were well pleased to play with me and to know that I had not lost anything concerning my style and ideas as most…

We met there a nice young man, Doug Hague, who was a great jazz fan and also a jazz critic for different reviews in the States and in England. He was there with his young Italian wife and his parents. Albert and Peggy Hague. They had some juice with them in a bag and they kept on asking us questions about France and telling us how much they loved that country and its way of life. Peggy was of French descendance and vaguely related with a member of the Hot Club de France, Jacques Morgantini from Pau. We became…

We left New York aboard the Liberte again on the first day of May and arrived in France and back home in Paris the 7th of May. I went back to the Trois Mailletz and did galas. There was a big jazz festival in Cannes the month of July and I was invited the 13th to play a jam session with Sydney Bechet, Roy "Little Jazz" Eldridge, Joe Turner the pianist and Teddy Buckner, whom I met for the first time. Whoever the rest of the musicians were, I don't remember, but they were not Americans.
